title: Board contract items for seven vendors, with the date of the meeting and the earliest date the item gives for the work
question: When the Board of Education was asked to act on these contracts, had the work, or the district’s own processing of the contract, already begun?
finding: 116 item pages were saved; 115 ask the board to act (107 on the consent calendar, 8 as separate items). None of the 115 pages records a vote or an outcome; the official minutes of 27 of the meetings were saved on 22 November 2026 and give the outcome of 53 of these items (screen board-votes-from-minutes). 75 pages give a date for the work or for processing, and in 74 of them that date comes before the meeting, by a median of 45 days. 67 are list items titled as contracts “processed between” two dates; the window closes a median of 18 days before the meeting (at most 60), and 33 of these lists are titled as ratifications.
how: Each saved item page (BoardDocs BD-GetAgendaItem, as text) is read for its meeting, type, subject and dollar amount, and for dates of the work: a stated service start ("Services were received ... beginning on"), a corrected term, "Term of Services", or the processing window in the title. The earliest of these is set against the meeting date. Vendors come from the puller’s table by item id.
limits: A meeting date is the date the item was on the agenda, not proof of a vote: an item can be pulled, continued or amended. The minutes on disk cover 27 meetings; for items at the other meetings the outcome is not on disk. “Processed” is the district’s word for its internal routing, not a signature or a start of work. Ratification of contracts under the bid limit after the fact is what the board’s rules provide for, and a list approved weeks after processing is the ordinary monthly calendar. The seven vendors were chosen by the owner, so the items are not a sample of all contracts.
